orders.text:
CRLA No. 432 of 2021
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Naman Kamboj, Advocate 
for the appellant.
Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, A.G.A for 
the State.
This matter is heard through 
Video Conferencing.
Appellant Amit Parley has been 
convicted and sentenced in Sessions 
Trial No. 144 of 2018, by the Court of 
4th Additional Sessions Judge, 
Dehradun. His appeal is pending. He 
has moved a short term bail 
application no. 2 of 2022 on the 
ground that the marriage of his 
cousin sister is to be held on 
18.02.2022. For the purposes of 
“bhat” ceremony, his presence 
necessary because there is no mail 
family member in his family.
Learned State counsel, under 
instruction, would submit that the 
marriage is settled on that date.
Without considering on merits, 
purely on the ground of marriage of 
the cousin sister of the appellant, the 
appellant may be enlarged on short 
term bail for six days subject to his 
furnishing a personal bond and two 
reliable sureties of the like amount, to 
the satisfaction of the court 
concerned.
After expiry of the period of 
short term bail, the appellant shall 
surrender before the court and an 
information shall be forwarded to this 
Court. The short term bail application
is allowed accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
Vacation Judge
 09.02.2022 Jitendra

IA No. 7 of 2022
In 
CRLA No. 432 of 2021
Hon’ble Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Mr. M. S. Bhandari, learned counsel 
holding brief of Mr. Naman Kamboj, learned 
counsel for the appellant. 
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General with Mr. Rakesh Kumar Joshi, 
learned Brief Holder for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
This application has been filed by the 
applicant – Amit Parley for extension of the 
short term bail. 
It is also noted that earlier occasion, the 
applicant has been granted short term bail on 
07.09.2022 by this Court on the ground that 
he was suffering from AC joint injury and he 
was recommended for treatment by surgical 
intervention. Thereafter, the surgical 
intervention was carried out on 28.10.2022.
Thereafter, on the submissions made by 
the learned counsel for the appellant, on the 
last date i.e. on 02.11.2022, seven days 
extension was granted to him with liberty to 
the appellant to file appropriate documents 
through an affidavit to extend the short term 
bail application granted by us to the applicant 
– Amit Parley. 
Today, in the Court, the learned counsel 
for the appellant files supplementary  affidavit, which is taken on record and the 
Registry is directed to register the same as an 
interim application. 
We have also perused the documents, 
especially the document appearing at Page 
No. 33 of the supplementary affidavit, which 
has been issued by the doctor on 07.11.2022
advising the appellant take rest, for post￾operation recovery, up to 24.11.2022.
In that view of the matter, we are 
inclined to allow the application for 
extension.
Interim bail, granted by us on 
07.09.2022, which was extended by us for 
another seven days on 02.11.2022 is hereby 
extended till 28.11.2022 on the same bail 
bond executed by the appellant before the 
learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, 
Dehradun. 
The application (IA No. 07 of 2022) for 
extension of short term bail is allowed. 
Let the applicant – Amit Parley 
surrender before the Court on 29.11.2022. To 
that extent, the time extension application is 
allowed and this order may be read as part of 
the original order passed by us on 
07.09.2022.
List this matter on 28.02.2023 for final 
disposal.
 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.) 
09.11.2022
(Grant urgent certified copy of this order, during course of the day, as per Rules)
A/-

20.11.2024 Short Term Bail Application No. IA/12/2024
In
CRLA No. 432 of 2021
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Naman Kamboj, learned counsel for the 
appellant and Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy 
Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand.
2. The appellant has challenged the judgment 
and order dated 02.09.2021 passed by 4th
Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun, District 
Dehradun in Sessions Trial No. 144 of 2018, 
whereby he has been convicted for offences 
punishable under Sections 302, 201 and 120B IPC 
and sentenced to life imprisonment.
3. Today, the matter is listed on Short Term 
Bail Application (IA/12/2024). Appellant has 
sought short term bail on the ground that the 
marriage of his cousin sister is scheduled to be 
solemnized on 22.11.2024. It is contended that 
there is no male member in the family of his 
cousin and appellant’s presence is necessary for 
performing ‘Bhaat’ ceremony, which is customary 
ritual in western Uttar Pradesh, where appellant’s 
family resides.
4. Learned State counsel was asked to get 
instructions. On instructions, he submits that there 
is marriage of appellant’s cousin sister on 
22.11.2024 and he also endorses the statement 
made by the appellant that there is no male 
member in the family of his cousin sister who can 
perform ‘Bhaat’ ceremony.
5. Having regard to the aforesaid facts, we are 
inclined to grant short term bail for a period of one 
week to the appellant.
6. Accordingly, the short term bail application 
is allowed. 7. Let the appellant-Amit Parley be enlarged on 
short term bail only for a period of one week from 
the date of his release, on his executing personal 
bond with two reliable sureties, each of the like 
amount, to the satisfaction of the Court 
concerned. 
8. Needless to say that immediately after 
expiry of one week, appellant shall surrender 
before the Superintendent of the Jail concerned. 
9. List this appeal in due course.
10. Let a certified copy of this order be issued 
today itself.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.) 
 20.11.2024

 Versus

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel for the 
appellant in CRLA No.287 of 2021 and Mr. M. K. Ray, 
learned Amicus Curiae for the appellant in CRLA No.432 of 
2021. 
2. Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, learned A.G.A for the State. 
3. Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and 
order dated 31.08.2021/02.09.2021, passed in Sessions Trial 
No.144 of 2018, State vs. Snehlata Chauhan & Anr., by the 
court of learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun. By 
it, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 302, 201 
and 120-B of IPC. 
4. The appellant, Snehlata Chauhan seeks short term bail 
on the ground that her two children are suffering from 
depression and the younger one has to be admitted in Class 
10th as he did not write his examination last year.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that 
appellant's two children, Sarthak Chauhan and Shaurya 
Pratap Singh Chauhan, are staying with their grandmother 
and grandfather; they are suffering from depression. The 
Child Welfare Committee, District Dehradun on 12.06.2026 
had given a report to that effect. The children are passing 
through psychological trauma due to the loss of their father 
and mother being in jail. Therefore, it is argued that the 
appellant may be released on short-term bail for some time  so that she could get her younger son admitted in Class 10th
and give them some company so that they could be 
emotionally a little strong to wade through their life.
6. Learned State counsel is required to get a report. 
Learned State Counsel submits that in fact the children of the 
appellant, Snehlata Chauhan, are staying with her parents.
There is no material on record to controvert the report of 
Child Welfare Committee, which is Annexure-2 to the short￾term bail application.
7. We have carefully gone through the CWC report, 
which records that the children of the appellant are suffering 
from depression and they are also going through emotional 
trauma. The report also records that if timely guidance is not 
given, the possibility of their coming into contact with anti￾social elements may not be ruled out.
8. Having considered, purely on humanitarian ground, 
the short term bail is granted to the appellant Snehlata 
Chauhan for a period of three weeks from the date of her
release, subject to her executing a personal bond and 
furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to 
the satisfaction of the court concerned. 
9. It is further directed that on expiry of the duration of 
short term bail, the appellant shall surrender before the court 
concerned.
10. List these matters on 04.11.2026
11. Let a copy of this order be immediately forwarded to 
the court and jail concerned through e-mail with a request 
that after obtaining e-true copy of it, necessary action may be 
initiated so that the release of the appellant is not delayed. 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 16.09.2026
Akash
